cards.q: What is OSPFv3 and its RFC?
cards.a: OSPFv3 (RFC 5340) is OSPF for IPv6. It keeps the same core concepts as OSPFv2 - LSAs, LSDB, SPF, areas, DR/BDR - but decouples the protocol logic from IPv4, carrying addresses as prefix options in LSA payloads.

cards.q: What is the key difference in how OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 encode addresses in LSAs?
cards.a: OSPFv2 encodes addresses in the LSA header, while OSPFv3 carries addresses as prefix options in the LSA payload. This makes OSPFv3 address-family-independent and allows multiple IPv6 prefixes per link.

cards.q: How do OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 differ in authentication?
cards.a: OSPFv2 uses MD5/SHA/plaintext authentication carried in the header. OSPFv3 has no OSPF-native authentication and instead relies on IPv6 AH/ESP or IPsec.

cards.q: Does OSPFv3 still require a router ID even on IPv6-only networks?
cards.a: Yes, OSPFv3 still requires a 32-bit router-id in IPv4 format. If there is no IPv4 address present, you must manually configure the router-id or OSPF may not start.

cards.q: What are the default hello and dead intervals for OSPFv3?
cards.a: The same as OSPFv2: 10 seconds hello and 40 seconds dead on broadcast and point-to-point networks. Neighbor states and DR/BDR election are also identical to OSPFv2.

cards.q: Write the modern OSPFv3 address-family configuration.
cards.a: router ospf 1, address-family ipv6, router-id 1.1.1.1, then interface Gi0/1 under the address family, then exit-address-family. The legacy alternative is interface Gi0/1 with ipv6 ospf 1 area 0.

cards.q: What global IPv6 feature must be enabled or OSPFv3 will not work?
cards.a: ipv6 unicast-routing must be enabled globally, otherwise OSPFv3 cannot form neighbors or the network will not function.

cards.q: Why is the term 'multiple prefixes per link' significant in OSPFv3?
cards.a: Because the LSA is address-family-independent, a single LSDB can serve any number of IPv6 prefixes on a link, and future address families (like IPv4 within OSPFv3) become possible without a new protocol.

cards.q: What show commands verify OSPFv3 operation?
cards.a: show ospf neighbor, show ospf interface, show ipv6 route ospf, and show ospf database.

cards.q: If OSPFv3 will not start, what is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A missing router-id is the most likely cause. Set the router-id with the router-id command. Also check that ipv6 unicast-routing is enabled and hello parameters match.

cards.q: How does OSPFv3 authenticate on the exam?
cards.a: OSPFv3 uses IPv6 AH/ESP or IPsec - there is no OSPF-native authentication. This differs from OSPFv2 which uses MD5/SHA/plaintext in the header.

cards.q: What is OSPFv3's RFC, address family, and authentication method?
cards.a: RFC 5340, address family IPv6, LSA addresses as prefix options in the payload, multiple prefixes per link yes, router ID 32-bit still required, auth IPv6 AH/ESP/IPsec, hello/dead 10/40 seconds, config via address-family ipv6, IPv4 twin is OSPFv2.
